rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grep zero-tolerance: no honest, delve, landscape, importantly, crucial, substrate, leverage(v), synergize, paradigm shift found in body region (lines 1-28, 32-96). No em-dashes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No ritual, ceremony, or practice(n) ambient usage found in body. No hard-ban violations.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No stale markers, "fixed" retrospectives, dated session references, or biography detected in body region. No transitions like relocated, moved, renamed, used to, previously.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 body registers correctly: Boris-flat on mechanics ("The access-control-analysis skill was installed as a personal skill during prework, so Claude Code auto-discovers it by name"); peer-warmth Godin register ("your own knowledge of the codebase flags", "your read"); Rory-style reframe ("STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling"). Voice quintet appropriate for engineer audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an exercise file, not an article draft. Rule applies to article surfaces only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique. Training creator's name banned in student-facing body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No creator names (Antti, the creator, the author, course creator, training creator) found in body. No named techniques paraphrased without credit. STRIDE and access-control-analysis credited implicitly through naming and exercise structure. No author-we detected.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body consistently uses "you" ("You invoke", "you should see", "your read", "your own knowledge"). No "the student" found. No delivery mechanics ("the trainer shows", "before students start") in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No maintainer-specific terms (self-compound, substrate, three-pattern, grill-me) found leaking into body. Terms used (access-control-analysis, delta, breadth walk) are all defined or referenced explicitly in the exercise context.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped sentences found (no "fine way to", "it's OK if", "no penalty", "not a box-check"). Delegation shapes (skill does breadth walk, student reads result) carry structure without defensive reassurance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an exercise file, not a reference artifact. Rule applies to reference surfaces only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named practitioners credited in body. STRIDE framework referenced by name once in "The point:" header. Access-control-analysis skill named as the artifact doing the work, not as a named practitioner.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Punchy line: "STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling." No carve-out needed; framing holds across the exercise scope without overpromising. The exercise design matches the claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No value-prop or defensive positioning detected. No phrases like "not an aspirational X", "not a vendor Y", "this isn't marketing", "the real practitioners", "grounded in actual". Teaching the move, not defending it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Jargon arrives at or before the point it earns: "Claude Code" introduced naturally as the tool student is using; "delta" explained in context ("the delta only you can add", explicitly contrasted with skill output); "breadth walk" appears with explanation context (skill's job). No L3-judgment terms planted before earned.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No dangling pronouns or bypass-the-agent punchlines in closers. Sections end on concrete next moves ("run the skill", "point the skill at your feature", "add the context header") or phase transitions, not on vague states.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The "What happened:" block is OPTIONAL.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File does not contain a "What happened:" section. Rule applies to exercises that include this optional block only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Verbs are peer-flat or warmer: "ask", "invoke", "point". No combative verbs (bark, order, command, whip, force, drag, push around, boss, shout at, snap at, lecture, scold) found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All headers are literally true: "Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk" = actual prompt instruction; "Phase 1: Run the curated skill" = accurate description of what happens; "Phase 2: Read the map back before you decide the delta" = accurate sequence; "Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed" = precise mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negations, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, or citation duplication. Prose is lean and action-forward. Example: "You invoke; the skill does the breadth walk" is direct without deictic waste.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "the two or three entries your own knowledge of the codebase flags" is a count distant from any list (used as memory handle for recall, not restating adjacent structure). No false adjacency counts found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Slogan: "STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling." Test: overstates? No — it is literally true that STRIDE without an access-surface map produces lower-quality threat models. Superlative holds within scope of this exercise's design.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No stamped claims in body region. Exercise references M1 pattern and Module 2's plan-path, but these are forward references / architectural mentions, not claims needing cross-verification.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an evaluation at a single point in time. Rule applies to multi-file sweeps that cache rule sets; not in scope for single-file instance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise names what student becomes: "your read is the short list" + "the delta only you can add" = student as contributor of codebase-specific insight. Never frames as corrective ("you're missing X"). Peer framing throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Technical terms earned or assumed-known per AE101 audience: 'Claude Code' is the platform in use; 'personal skill' explained via context ("installed as a personal skill during prework, so Claude Code auto-discovers it by name"); 'context' and 'context-load status' self-evident in Claude Code setting; 'delta' earned in opening ("the delta only you can add").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No narrating student's past or present state.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No patronizing past narration like "You've done the work" or present-state ascription like "you are waiting". Body focuses on what student IS DOING ("You invoke", "You should see", "Pick the feature") not what they HAVE done or ARE in the moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No scheduling the student's attention.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No consumption-guidance lines scheduling when to read or return to material. "Check back where the prework extracted the bundle" is point-of-use reference, not scheduling attention. Student authority preserved.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No overclaim of student verification or coverage.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No claims of full verification beyond what the exercise asks for. Phase 3 asks for delta entries, not exhaustive coverage. No "audit the entire map" or full-coverage claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No contemplative-pause theatre or room-share commands.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "Sit with", "Take a moment", "Pause", "breathe", "Let it land", "tell the room", "Say out loud", "call it out", "Share with", or similar performance-cue language. Hard-grep phrase list: all clear.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consistent second-person throughout ("You invoke", "You should see", "your read", "your own knowledge", "You decide"). No third-person "the student" or trainer-POV delivery mechanics in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No maintainer-only terms detected (self-compound, substrate, three-pattern, grill-me). Terms used are all transparent to exercise context.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance phrases detected. Delegation structure ("the skill does the breadth walk; you read the result") carries confidence without defensive appending.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is not a simulation exercise. Rule applies to self-study simulation surfaces only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No callout boxes of that shape. Citations to STRIDE and access-control-analysis integrated naturally into exercise flow.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All student moves are chat-based ("Ask Claude to list", "Ask Claude to invoke", "ask Claude to integrate", "add the surface"). No editor/terminal forcing function outside the agent conversation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No CLAUDE.md references in body prose. Rule applies only where file mentions CLAUDE.md layer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No em-dashes found in body. Sentences are simple and clear. Complex ideas broken into short sentences ("You invoke; the skill does the breadth walk.") rather than em-dash compounds.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers use command/action verbs: "Take the ranked ten" (imperative), "Run the curated skill" (imperative), "Point the skill at your feature" (imperative), "Kick off the pass" (imperative), "Read the map back" (imperative), "Add the surface" (imperative), "Push back until" (imperative), "Add the context header" (imperative). All headers align with student actions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No inline cross-curriculum links in body region. One reference to "Module 2's close" is described, not linked.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Claude Code" used consistently throughout as the platform/tool; no collision with student's own authored code. "The skill" (curated tool) vs "Skills you author later" clearly distinguished by context. No ambiguity where student writes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Vocabulary correct: 'the agent' for acting/execution ("the skill does the breadth walk"), 'Claude' for addressee/product ("Ask Claude to", "Claude narrates", "Claude Code"), 'the agent' for multi-step work ("invoke the access-control-analysis skill as a subagent"). No conflation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Task/session terminology correct: "in the m3-security session", "the session", "one sitting". No noun-run usage in student-facing body. Terminology aligns with vocabulary.md registry.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No time-of-day anchors detected (tomorrow, overnight, this morning, tonight, next morning, yesterday, last night). Only phase timing markers ("7 min", "3 min") which are appropriate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No labeled reflection moments like "Pause before you", "Meta-moment", "Step back", "let it land". Reflection happens within natural phase transitions (Phase 2 walk-through, Phase 3 delta decision) without theater framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts ask Claude to invoke and save; then walk the map back; then integrate deltas. No meta-loops asking student to restate prior decisions. Student decides in chat, Claude proposes, student steers — no redundant asks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: ".md" is default file type for student artifacts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File itself is .md format. No body prose specifying file type for student artifacts (saving prompts live in fenced prompt blocks, not body). Rule applies where body directs artifact file type only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prose is lean with high NVA-test passage rate. Every sentence advances the student's understanding or action. No implementation detail before point-of-use; no extra source trivia; maintainer reasoning does not leak into body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts route output to disk, then body directs next moves ("walk you through the map", "decide which surface", "add the context header") rather than narrating read. No generic "read it" or "look at it" after output descriptions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Forward callout at close: "What this sets up" names what student will do next ("The STRIDE exercise invokes the curated STRIDE skill on the map you just built.") Student as subject of future capability, not audience-shifted role.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Operational settings (m3-security session, Claude Code, personal skills) restated at point of use ("in the m3-security session", "In the Claude Code chat, type:") as well as introduced. No reliance on prework-only recall.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Uses training vocabulary: 'the loop' context (M1 countermove), 'the move' (standard house frame), 'steering', no invented synonyms. Vocabulary aligns with AE101 spine.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body names prompt as artifact ("Ask Claude to list...", "the surface map file") rather than describing typing (no "type", "tell it", "say to Claude"). Vocabulary treats prompts as house noun for student utterances.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Outcome named: "Claude Code auto-discovers it by name" rather than recipe for discovery. "See what skills your Claude has loaded" asks for state, not mechanics. Level appropriate for engineer audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No arc-positioning or module-narration in body. Subject of sentences is student/artifact/task, not the training's shape. No forward-callout describing where module sits in arc; only forward-callout names what student will do next (STRIDE exercise).
